passages.note: His newsletter reports a study on the costs of the 2025 tariffs, which leans against escalating tariffs but names no policy (reduce most, eliminate all, or keep selective tariffs), so it does not separate the rungs on that side.

rows.reasoning: In his July 2026 newsletter, Pierce reports that 'The average Hoosier household had its costs raised by $2,600' and that Indiana lost manufacturing jobs because of the 2025 tariffs. That criticism leans away from 'increase tariffs on countries that don't trade fairly' and 'impose high tariffs on all imports', but he never says whether tariffs should be eliminated, mostly reduced, or used selectively, so no rung's clauses are matched.

quotes.text: The average Hoosier household had its costs raised by $2,600. There were 9,148 fewer manufacturing jobs in Indiana because of the tariffs.
